condition: acute agricultural insecticide poisoning in an apple orchard farmworker presenting with abrupt profuse continuous salivation 20 minutes after spraying insecticide on apple trees
level_rationale: Abrupt onset of profuse continuous salivation pouring from the mouth 20 minutes ago in a 41-year-old farmworker who sprayed insecticide on apple trees today indicates acute muscarinic cholinergic insecticide toxicity carrying imminent risks of bronchorrhea, bronchospasm, neuromuscular paralysis, and respiratory arrest requiring immediate emergency department airway protection, decontamination, and parenteral atropine therapy, whereas feeling mild mouth dryness for 10 minutes this afternoon after orchard work reflects minor transient thirst manageable with home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain low-literacy farmworker lexical register swap (-reg) + uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A same-mouth brief mild dryness self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (41-year-old farmworker, spraying insecticide on apple trees today, and nonstop profuse salivation pouring from the mouth 20 minutes ago) with zero apostrophe contractions and a 1-word span difference (10 vs 11 words). Keeping 'my mouth' identical in f3 avoids adding any unstated body site and leaves zero dermal spill stranded when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to 10 minutes of mild mouth dryness this afternoon (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
